text:
At dawn, when the hawk stirs, moved by pleasure and nobility, the thrush leaps and cries joyfully, greeting his beloved in the brush, I wish to offer you—and tremble impatiently to do so—the sweetness due a lover. Know Love has written it in his book. This is the end to which God calls us.

You will always be mistress of my life, wholly, until my death: gentle laurel of my soul's dream, noble olive grove cooling Bitterness. Reason commands the fire endure (in this I follow its decree) that drives me toward you though it seem blind. This is the end to which God calls us.

When sorrow advances on me, when Fortune casts torment at me, your sweet, serene gaze dispels them as wind dispels smoke. I do not lose what I sow in you, for the fruit declares it will be mine. God asks it: I will keep cultivating you. This is the end to which God calls us. Hear, Princess, what my longing cries: my heart claims you forever. From you I hope the same constancy. This is the end to which God calls us.

translation.title: Ballad to His Lady for Robert d'Estouteville
